clue.text: Take some time next to counter in New York — it'll help you get your words right

definitions.text: it'll help you get your words right

parts.note: a spell is a period of time, so taking some time is having a spell
in American English a checker is a draughts piece, a playing counter

explanation.surface: Instructions to linger at a shop counter in Manhattan, oddly promising better writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' simply joins the two pieces. Americans call draughts checkers, so a checker is one of the counters.
explanation.definitionFit: A software tool that flags misspelt words exists precisely to help a writer get their words right.

clue.text: Avian predator ignoring unusually large target

indicators.note: ignoring says those letters are left out

parts.note: an osprey is a large fish-eating hawk
OS stands for outsize, unusually large

explanation.surface: A hunting bird passes over an oversized quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Prey is the creature a hunter aims at, its quarry or target.

clue.text: Left pair of Americans either side of IT chief (very attractive)

indicators.note: either side of says the two copies flank the next piece

parts.note: US stands for the Americans, and a pair gives it twice
CIO is a chief information officer, the head of IT

explanation.surface: Two Americans flank the head of tech, who is described as very good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Luscious describes something richly appealing to the senses, especially a very attractive person.

clue.text: Minister heading for Uruguay aboard plane

indicators.note: aboard says that letter goes inside the vehicle

parts.note: crate is slang for an old aircraft

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A government minister flies to Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political but means a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant member of the clergy, and ministers of religion are clergy.

clue.text: A lot of cows going through border of field, heading off exhilaration

indicators.note: going through says the shortened word for cows passes inside the other piece
heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a fence marks the edge of a field

indicators.note: a lot of says most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them, so cows means bullies

explanation.surface: A herd of cattle pushes through a field's boundary, causing excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cows' looks like cattle but is the verb meaning intimidates. 'A lot of' and 'heading off' each trim a piece, one at its end, the other at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebullience is bubbling high spirits, close in meaning to exhilaration.

clue.text: Questing king, late in the day, to slip up with soldier — ready to lose heart

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
night comes late in the day
to err is to slip up
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: to lose heart says the middle of the word drops out, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A late-night monarch on a quest stumbles alongside a soldier who is ready but downhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Knight-errantry was the medieval practice of roaming in search of adventure, the questing life.

clue.text: Clever, not needing book to be correct

indicators.note: not needing says the letter is removed

parts.note: bright means clever

explanation.surface: A smart student does not need a textbook to get answers right.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are synonyms for being accurate or free from error.

clue.text: Trainee not quite joining reduced staff in crime busting force

indicators.note: not quite says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an intern is a trainee

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a pole is a staff or rod

explanation.surface: An apprentice joins a cut-back team at a police agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but means a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation that helps forces cooperate against crime.

clue.text: Collection of art college held in it, in modest, largely decorated surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says this word goes round what has been built, with 'in' as a link

parts.note: pure can mean chaste or modest

indicators.note: held in says the letter goes inside the word it
decorated says the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: An art college's collection is kept in a modest but ornately trimmed building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' looks like 'mostly', but it is the anagram fodder for 'decorated'; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture gallery is a room or building where a collection of paintings is shown.

clue.text: Rumour first group is out of time

parts.note: first is number one, written NO I with I as the Roman one

indicators.note: out of says the letter for time is taken away from the pieces before it

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that the leading band are no longer keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is just a link. NO I (number one) plus SET makes NOISET, and 'out of time' removes the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise in the sense of talk or report going around, as in noises being made about something, is rumour.

clue.text: Blossoming in the growing season?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: spring is the season when plants start to grow
flowers that are blossoming are out

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about flowers opening up during the spring months.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition, since plants put out shoots in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprouting is putting out new shoots and buds, the kind of flourishing typical of spring.

clue.text: Takes in some fare at supper?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner consumes part of the food served at the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Takes' alone as the definition; the phrase 'Takes in' is what means eats, so 'in' belongs to the definition rather than being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to consume it, and eats is the plain synonym for consumes.

clue.text: "Consuming a good deal in drink, tumbling over, getting angry" — report

indicators.note: tumbling over says the combined letters are turned round and read backwards
consuming says the drink swallows up the next piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: to sip is to drink
lots means a good deal
hot under the collar is angry, so getting angry is getting hot

explanation.surface: A quoted account of someone drinking heavily, falling down and losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consuming' and 'tumbling over' together make PISTOLS. 'report' looks like a written account but is the bang of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud explosive sound, so a gun being fired produces one.

clue.text: Ailing guy, with poorly body, always neglecting variable item of medical data

indicators.note: ailing means sick, so these letters are in a poor state and get rearranged
always neglecting says every occurrence of the letter is left out, not just one

parts.note: Y is a classic algebraic variable; all three in the fodder go

explanation.surface: A sick man in poor physical shape keeps forgetting a changeable entry in his medical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: GUY, POORLY and BODY each hold a Y; 'always neglecting' drops all three, and 'Ailing' rearranges the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's blood type, such as O or AB, is one of the facts kept in medical records.

clue.text: Our pile's wobbly, threatening

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Our heap of belongings is unsteady and looks ready to topple.
explanation.definitionFit: Perilous means full of danger, and something dangerous is threatening.

clue.text: Salad vegetable, mostly picked, over beside railway

indicators.note: over says the shortened word is turned back to front
mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: elect means picked or chosen

explanation.surface: A salad ingredient, mostly chosen, sitting next to a train line.
explanation.walkthrough: ELECT without its last letter is ELEC, which 'over' reverses to CELE.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crunchy stalked vegetable often eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: People farming English manor redeployed in yards?

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the yards

parts.note: Y is short for yard, so two yards are YY

indicators.note: redeployed says the letters are moved to new positions

explanation.surface: Farmhands from an English country estate are moved around into yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were small landowners who farmed their own land, and yeomanry is them as a class.

clue.text: Cultural note abandoned in representation of coastline

indicators.note: representation of says the letters are rendered in a different form
abandoned says that letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: A painter leaves out a musical note in depicting the coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society and its ways, which overlaps with cultural.

clue.text: Lake city in USA — really?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
'go on!' is an exclamation of disbelief, like 'really?'

explanation.surface: A doubtful reaction to someone claiming an American city sits on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of salt water cut off from the sea, a kind of small lake.

clue.text: Expression of wonder about note a sure thing in virtuoso piece

indicators.note: about says the exclamation goes round the pieces that follow

parts.note: coo! is an exclamation of surprise or wonder
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A gasp of admiration greets a guaranteed showstopper in a dazzling solo performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here: the note and the sure thing sit together inside the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a showpiece for a solo instrument, often written to display the player's virtuosity.

clue.text: Host bringing in beer, also carrying British wine

indicators.note: bringing in says the host takes the rest inside

parts.note: MC is master of ceremonies, a host

indicators.note: carrying says the beer holds the letter inside it

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A host serves beer and also British wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'also' is just a link between the two container steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Malbec is a red grape variety and the red wine made from it.

clue.text: Get Phi calm, unusually calm

indicators.note: unusually says these letters are arranged in an unexpected way

explanation.surface: The setter asks for help staying unusually composed.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is this puzzle's setter, writing himself into the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegmatic describes a temperament that stays unemotional and unruffled, which is calm.

clue.text: Courtyard — work to surround it with area that's elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated says the letters are read from bottom to top
to surround says the work goes round the next pieces

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Raised paving work encloses an outdoor yard.
explanation.walkthrough: The container gives OITAP, and 'that's elevated' turns it upward, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area next to a house, like a small courtyard.

clue.text: Member of ancient culture in Central America

parts.note: CA is short for Central America

explanation.surface: Describes someone from an old civilisation living in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places this culture in Central America; the Incas were in fact from the Andes of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people of a pre-Columbian empire, so an Inca belongs to that ancient culture.

clue.text: This has nothing on marine fish producer?

parts.note: FA, as in sweet FA, means nothing
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: Something with no hold over a fish breeder in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This has' means the answer is made of what follows; in a down clue 'on' puts one piece above the other. The question mark flags a fish farm as one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm rears fish for food, so a farm can produce fish.

clue.text: That chap has reduced interest in bird book set in fabulous land

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces go inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
he refers to that chap

indicators.note: reduced says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hobby is an interest

explanation.surface: A man with fewer interests in birds owns a fantasy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'interest' means a pastime, not money earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's novel is set in Middle-earth, an imaginary world of dragons and wizards.

clue.text: Kitchen item increasingly just overlooked at first

indicators.note: overlooked at first says the opening letter is left out

parts.note: fairer means more just

explanation.surface: A household appliance that gets ever fairer, though people ignore it initially.
explanation.walkthrough: A clothes airer is a rack for drying laundry, often kept in British kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes airer is a folding drying rack commonly stood in the kitchen.

clue.text: Sports blazer

parts.note: not a jacket worn for sport but something that blazes at a sporting event

explanation.surface: Looks like a jacket with a club badge.
explanation.walkthrough: A blazer is a jacket, but also anything that blazes; the torch lit at the Games is the latter.
explanation.definitionFit: The flame burns throughout the Games, literally a fire blazing over a sporting event.
